newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian March ANZ job ads series falls 1.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Australian March ANZ job ads series falls 1.9 pct.

text.p: The Australian and New Zealand (ANZ) Banking Group said on Monday its job advertisement series fell by 1.9 percent in March, after having risen by 3.3 percent and 1.8 percent in January and February respectively.
The level of job ads was down 9.4 percent on last March.
In trend terms, job ads rose 0.4 percent in the month, their fourth successive rise. The trend level of job ads was 8.5 percent lower than in March last year.

ANZ chief economist Saul Eslake said the March decline might have been at least partly due to the Easter break falling entirely in March, although he said there was no clear guidance from previous instances as to how marked the effect might be.
"Nevertheless, the underlying upward trend in job ads remains intact, consistent with the notion that a modest recovery in the demand for labour is now underway," Eslake said in a statement.

"Indeed, despite last month's minor setback, the trend in job advertising over the past three months is broadly consistent with net new job creation averaging around 15,000 per month during the June quarter, a slight improvement on the outlook suggested by earlier data," Eslake said.

However, downward revisions to previous official employment data and the 7,200 fall in February job levels meant this rate of growth would no longer be sufficent to meet the government's budget forecast, as the ANZ had suggested last month, he said.
The government has forecast employment growth in 1996/97 (July-June) of 1.5 percent, which would require average jobs growth of at least 28,000 per month between March and June, he said.
Job advertisements fell in every state except New South wakes, where they rose 3.1 percent.
The largest fall was in the Australian Capital Territory where job ads fell 19.4 percent, reversing large increases in the previous two months.
